Work included constructing a new chiller building, installing modern hydronic piping systems, replacing the main Emergency Department air handler (Air Handlining Unit (AHU-1)), upgrading electrical systems, and converting the Emergency Department wing from electric reheat to hydronic heating and cooling. Commissioning, testing, adjusting, and balancing were completed under this grant. These upgrades improve energy efficiency, operational resilience, and system reliability while preparing the campus for future electrification and renewable energy integration. They also support growth in healthcare services for a rural population. The project directly reduces energy costs and provides a foundation for future decarbonization measures, including a FEMA-funded microgrid and a large-scale ground source heat pump (GSHP) project. These follow-on initiatives would not have been possible without the hydronic backbone built through this project. Introduction Klickitat Valley Health operates critical healthcare infrastructure for a rural community in south-central Washington State. Prior to this project, much of the HVAC and central plant infrastructure relied on outdated, inefficient, and less resilient technology. This modernization addressed aging infrastructure while enabling future decarbonization, resiliency, and efficiency goals. The project focused on: - Replacing obsolete chiller equipment and converting portions of the heating distribution system from electric reheat to hydronic. - Installing an efficient, flexible hydronic backbone to enable future electrification and low-carbon heating and cooling. - Improving reliability and patient comfort while supporting growth in patient services. Background The legacy central utility plant did not meet modern efficiency or reliability standards and constrained future expansion and carbon reduction. KVH sought to optimize heating and cooling operations and create infrastructure capable of integrating advanced clean energy technologies. This project was part of KVH’s broader strategy to: - Achieve carbon neutrality and climate resilience in healthcare operations. - Electrify heating and cooling loads using modern, flexible systems. - Prepare for integration with on-site renewable generation microgrid and a ground source heat pump system. 4 DE-EE0010150 Results and Discussion 1. Finalize System Design and Permitting – 100% design drawings approved, City and DOH permits secured. 2. Procurement & Delivery of Equipment – Air handler, chillers, hydronic piping, and associated electrical components procured. 3. Installation – New chiller plant, cooling towers, and piping installed; hydronic distribution tied to AHU-1. 4. Start-up & Commissioning – All systems tested, balanced, and commissioned. 5. Permit Close-out – All inspections passed, permits closed by June 16, 2025. Key Achievements - Constructed new chiller building and installed modern chillers. - Converted Emergency Department wing from electric reheat to hydronic heating. - Upgraded main Emergency Department air handler (AHU-1). - Installed a campus-wide hydronic backbone enabling future electrification. - Integrated the new equipment into our Building Automation System. - Commissioned and balanced all new systems for operational readiness. 5 DE-EE0010150
